title: Tie the camel, then trust
hook: no soul dies until its provision is complete (Ibn Majah)
carry: rizq is written: tie the camel, then trust
tomorrow: dad and Amira snap over the dishes. what did the Prophet do at home?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the body's right: rest, paid like a wage. Today, the worry that keeps people from resting at all. Money.

An envelope on the kitchen counter, opened, then folded back up. A financial aid letter, with a gap where the number should have been bigger. Somebody at home says the old line: your rizq is written. Your provision. So if it's written, why try at all? The question is old, and so is the line. It comes from a hadith in Sunan Ibn Majah: no soul will die until it has received its provision in full.
screen: `A GAP IN THE LETTER.` → `YOUR RIZQ IS WRITTEN.` → `SO WHY TRY?`

segments.voice: Hear the whole report first. The Prophet ﷺ said: fear God and be gentle in seeking. No soul dies until it has its full provision, even if it comes slowly. So take what is lawful and leave what is forbidden. The Qur'an says it of every creature. In Pickthall's words: "And there is not a beast in the earth but the sustenance thereof dependeth on Allah." Now two readings, both inside the tradition. The first leans on trust. Another hadith says that if you relied on God as you truly should, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they go out hungry in the morning and come back full. Some readers hear that and say: loosen your grip. The scramble itself is the problem. The second leans on effort. A man asked the Prophet: should I tie my camel and trust God, or leave her loose and trust? Tie her, he said, and trust. Effort isn't a lack of faith; it's part of it. And look again at the birds. They don't wait in the nest. They go out. Both readings agree on the thing to drop: the panic. Written doesn't mean stop applying. It means the worry gets smaller than the work. One for tonight: in the hadith of the birds, the trusting ones are the ones who leave home early.
screen: `BE GENTLE IN SEEKING.` · `EVERY CREATURE'S SUSTENANCE.` · `THE BIRDS GO OUT HUNGRY.` · `TIE HER, AND TRUST.` · then, large: `PROVISION IS WRITTEN.`

segments.voice: Name one money worry in a few words, in your head or on paper. Then name one thing that's yours to do this week, the tied camel, and one thing that isn't, the part you hand over. Some Muslims say hasbiyallah, God is enough for me, as they set that second part down.
screen: `ONE WORRY.` · `MINE TO DO.` · `NOT MINE: HANDED OVER.`

segments.voice: Provision is written: your rizq, what you're given to live on, is already measured. You still go out to seek it, gently.
Pocket this: rizq is written, so tie the camel, then trust. That's ten of ten for work and money.

screen: `DAY 1711 COUNTS.` → `WORK AND MONEY · 10 OF 10.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT DID THE PROPHET DO AT HOME?`

howItsDone: Muslims speak of rizq, provision, as coming from God, and pair tawakkul, trust, with effort, as in the hadith 'tie her, and trust'; some say hasbiyallah when money worries press.
